control.title: Recommended control
control.description:
Rating: **{status_en}**

{advice_en}<!-- {status_hu} {advice_hu} -->

This is an engineering default, not a replacement for an installer's design.

data.confirm: I know this system is not recommended and accept it

data_description.control: TPI + PWM: switches the relay in pulses (on for a share of every cycle) by the error and the heat need – fits most relay boilers. PID + PWM: the same pulses with an integral, it does not stay below the target. External thermostat: HC only sets the target of an existing thermostat (a TRV, Better Thermostat, a Wi-Fi heater). AC – virtual i-Feel: HC moves the air conditioner's setpoint so that the room thermometer (not the unit's own sensor) reaches the target. On/off: plain on below / off above the target with long runs (heat pumps). Heating curve: flow temperature by the outdoor temperature.

entities.title: Entities
entities.description: A new instance always starts in shadow mode: it calculates but switches nothing. Only the fields on top are needed, the More part can be set later; where possible, I filled them in.

data.indoor_entity: Indoor temperature (optional when a wall thermostat contact is given)
data.flow_setpoint_entity: Flow setpoint entity (number / input_number, e.g. OpenTherm or ebusd)
data.demand_entity: Wired wall thermostat contact (optional: on = it asks for heat)

data_description.floor_entity: The thermometer in the floor. Required for electric floor heating: without it, or without a fresh reading, it does not heat.
data_description.demand_entity: A dry-contact wall thermostat read through a binary sensor, input boolean or switch: on = heat, off = no heat; then the room thermometer is optional. Frost, window, summer rest, the floor limit and floor tempering still apply. Unavailable: the lost-sensor fallback.

more.name: More (optional)
more.description: Meters, a second heat source, floor, heat pump, target source. They can be set later in the settings too.

data.energy_factor: Heat per unit (Custom only: kWh per metered unit)
data.extra_heat_entity: Other heat source energy (cumulative, e.g. air conditioner)
data.extra_factor: Heat per unit of the other source (e.g. COP)
data.boiler_power_kw: Boiler output (0 = heat need is not used in regulation)
data.zone_temp_entity: Adjoining room thermometer (e.g. a conservatory or the next room)
data.zone_max_diff: Counts as part of the house if at most this much colder
data.valve_feedback_entity: Valve feedback (end switch or valve position, if there is one)
data.floor_max: Floor temperature limit (0 = by covering and probe position)
data.floor_hysteresis: Back on this far below the limit
data.onoff_hysteresis: Switch on this far below the target
data.power_available_entity: Controlled power signal (optional: on = power available)
data.floor_temper: Floor tempering (keep the floor warm even when the room is warm enough)
data.floor_temper_offset: Floor target above the room target (0 = by the floor covering)
data.floor_temper_night: Floor target at night / in the sleep preset (0 = as by day)
data.floor_temper_hysteresis: Tempering back on this far below the floor target
data.floor_temper_room_margin: No tempering once the room is this much above its target
data.floor_fallback: Lost room thermometer: keep the floor warm by the floor sensor
data.heat_fuel: Fuel (the heat is worked out from it)

data_description.reference_entity: Used by fault detection and the shadow comparison. If empty, the relay or thermostat.
data_description.heat_energy_entity: The heat need is learned from these and the temperatures. It needs at least 3 whole days, statistics count too.
data_description.extra_factor: Heat per metered unit of the other source: for a heat pump or AC its COP (3 = 1 kWh of power gives 3 kWh of heat).
data_description.valve_feedback_entity: The central boiler uses it to see whether the valve is really open (on/off, open/closed or at least 20 %). Empty or unavailable: it counts with the actuator opening time.
data_description.floor_entity: The thermometer in the floor. Required for electric floor heating: without it, or without a fresh reading, it does not heat.
data_description.floor_max: No heat above it, whatever the regulator says. 0 = by the covering and the sensor position: under the covering 29 °C for tiles, 27 °C for wood, laminate, vinyl, carpet; in the screed between the pipes 29 / 33 / 31 (vinyl) °C; above a supply pipe 36 °C. An electric floor always uses the under-covering value. Without a covering: 27 °C for an electric floor, 29 °C for a water floor.
data_description.target_source_entity: When someone changes its target (e.g. on the wall thermostat's knob), this instance takes it over as a manual target until the next scheduled change. What HC writes there itself is not taken over.
data_description.hp_defrost_entity: While on (or named defrost), fault detection waits and the run does not count as running without command.
data_description.hp_dhw_entity: A 3-way valve or a mode sensor: while it makes hot water the house waits, this is no fault.
data_description.floor_temper: Comfort: a warm floor. While the room is warm enough the floor is held at the room target + the offset (by the floor sensor); it stops when the room gets this much above its target. The floor limit always wins. Needs a floor sensor.
data_description.floor_temper_room_margin: Default 0.5 °C. A larger value gives a warmer floor, but the room swings further above its target and uses more energy.
data_description.floor_fallback: Instead of the blind demand (or, for an electric floor, no heat) the floor is held at the room target + the tempering offset while the room thermometer is silent. Without a floor reading it works as before.
data_description.floor_covering: Gives the floor limit (with the sensor position) and the tempering offset: tiles 2 °C, other coverings 3 °C.
data_description.floor_probe: A sensor deeper in the screed reads warmer than the surface, so its limit is higher. The deeper positions' limits (screed 31–33 °C, above a pipe 36 °C) are estimates: they do not guarantee a surface below 27 °C. Under wood, parquet and laminate a sensor right under the covering (surface) is recommended.
data_description.heat_fuel: Automatic: from the meter's unit (m³ gas, kWh, MJ, GJ), without a meter from the heat source. Custom: the number below is kept. For a heat pump, Custom is right.
data_description.heat_efficiency: Counts for a burner (gas, oil, pellet); not for electric heat or a heat meter.

central.title: Central boiler
central.description: Switches the boiler by the demand of the chosen zone thermostats; waits for actuator valves to open. Starts in shadow mode. With a modulating boiler, the zone asking the most sets the flow by its own curve.

data.confirm: I understand: active mode switches a real device
data.central_keep_alive_s: Resend the boiler's on state every (s, 0 = off)
data.central_pump_overrun_s: Pump overrun after the boiler stops (0 = off)
data.central_pump_bypass: Bypass / always-open circuit (the overrun needs no open valve)
data.flow_setpoint_entity: Flow setpoint (modulating boiler, optional: number / input_number)
data.central_flow_default: Flow when no zone asks for a value
data.central_pump_exercise_s: Weekly pump exercise: run time (0 = off)
data.central_pump_exercise_idle_days: Only when the pump has stood still for (days)

data_description.central_pump_exercise_s: With a pump entity: a pump that stood still for days runs alone for this long once a week, so it does not seize. Only while the boiler is off and no zone asks; the boiler does not start; not in the first minutes after a restart.

buffer.title: Buffer tank
buffer.description: Switches the heat source (pellet, heat pump, electric element) by the tank thermometers: the top below the lower limit starts it, the tank charges up to the upper limit. With zones given a new charge only starts while a zone asks for heat. Starts in shadow mode.

data.buffer_demand_led: Start a new charge only on zone demand
data.buffer_on: Charge starts when the top is this cold or colder
data.buffer_off: Charge stops when the bottom (or the top) reaches
data.buffer_frost: Frost: charge when the top falls below

data_description.valve_delay_s: When the zone valve opens slowly (thermoelectric, ~5 minutes) or the pump is started late by its own control: heat starts this long after switching on. HC lengthens the run by it, the minimum on time counts the useful part, and demands too small for a run are carried into the next cycles. 0 = no delay.
data_description.min_on_s: The shortest useful run; with a delay set, a smaller demand is carried into the next cycle.

go_live.title: Go live: {name}
go_live.description:
In shadow mode HC calculates and logs what it would do, but switches nothing. Live, it switches the boiler relay (or sets the thermostat / AC unit, the TRV heads) itself.

Go live only when the shadow decisions looked right for a while and nothing else (a wall thermostat, an automation) controls the same output. Every other setting stays as it is.

go_shadow.description: HC keeps calculating and logging, but switches nothing from now on. The output stays as it is now – switch it by hand if needed.

regulation.name: Control and timing
regulation.description: Controller, cycle, minimum times, start holds, PID and curve parameters.

data.coast_window_s: Wait for the after-heat after a burn (0 = off)
data.pre_change_s: No new start before the target goes down (0 = off)
data.yield_margin: While the other (cheaper) source heats the coupled zone, the boiler regulates this much below the target (0 = off)
data.pid_ki_per_hour: PID integral gain (demand per °C per hour)
data.room_ki_per_hour: Room correction slow part (°C per °C per hour)
data.onoff_hysteresis: Switch on this far below the target
data.ac_ki_per_hour: AC: slow setpoint correction (°C per °C per hour)
data.ac_min_change_s: AC: minimum time between setpoint changes
data.assist_climate: House thermostat the AC helps when cheaper and the door is open (HC)
data.storage_discharge_hyst: Discharge starts this far below the target
data.fan_overrun_s: Fan overrun after the valve closes
data.fan_min_coil: The fan starts only above this coil temperature
data.keep_alive_s: Resend the on state every (s, 0 = off) – for a relay with its own auto-off timer

data_description.control: TPI: proportional pulses by the error and the outdoor temperature. PID: proportional + integral (+ derivative) – removes a lasting offset. Both drive the relay by PWM: on for a share of every cycle.
data_description.cycle_s: PWM cycle: one on + off period. The demand is the share of it the relay is on (50 % of 900 s = 7.5 minutes on).
data_description.min_on_s: Shortest burn: a shorter pulse is skipped or stretched (spares the boiler and the relay).
data_description.valve_delay_s: A slow thermoelectric valve (~5 min) or a pump started late: the run is lengthened by it, the minimum on time counts the useful part, small demands add up. 0 = none.
data_description.coast_window_s: For this long after a burn no new start while the room, just under the target, still rises (the radiators give their heat). Suggested: 2700 s. Off by default (measured on one house).
data_description.pwm_midcycle_start: When the demand grows past the minimum run in the middle of a cycle, a new cycle starts at once (no wait for the next). Off by default (measured on one house).
data_description.pwm_carry: Demands below the minimum run add up to a real run (always so with a valve delay). Off by default: in the simulation it raised the overshoot after a boost.
data_description.pre_change_s: This long before a scheduled lowering of the target (night start, a preset or manual target running out) no new burn starts while the room is already at or above the coming target – its heat would arrive after the change. A running burn is not cut. Default: 1800 s.
data_description.pid_kp: How strongly HC answers the error now (0.4 = 40 % demand per °C below the target).
data_description.pid_ki_per_hour: How fast a lasting error adds demand (per °C and hour).
data_description.pid_d_filter_s: Room sensors report in 0.1 °C steps, only on a change: an unfiltered derivative is spiky. 0 = no filter; only matters when the derivative gain is not 0.
data_description.keep_alive_script: When set, at every keep-alive of the relay that should stay on HC runs this script instead of switching the relay on again – for example a Shelly "turn on with a 15-minute flip-back timer". A long burn is then never cut, while a dead Home Assistant leaves the relay on for that long at most.

functions.description: Summer rest, boost, learning, taking over from a wall thermostat.

data.season_enabled: Summer rest by outdoor daily average
data.boost_enabled: Boost on a large deficit (accounts for after-heat)
data.learning_enabled: Learning (after-heat, boost time, TPI strength and holding offset)
data.shadow_regulator: Shadow regulator: the other algorithm (PID next to TPI) calculates too, switches nothing
data.adopt_manual: Adopt changes made on the managed thermostat
data.demand_entity: Wired wall thermostat contact (optional: on = it asks for heat)

data_description.adopt_manual: External control: a target set on the managed thermostat itself (not by HC) becomes the manual target until the next scheduled change; if someone switches it off, HC leaves it off (frost protection excepted) until someone switches it on again. Off: HC writes its own target and mode as before.
data_description.target_source_entity: When someone changes its target (e.g. on the wall thermostat's knob), this instance takes it over as a manual target until the next scheduled change. What HC writes there itself is not taken over.
data_description.demand_entity: A dry-contact wall thermostat read through a binary sensor, input boolean or switch: on = heat, off = no heat. Frost, window, summer rest, the floor limit and floor tempering still apply. Unavailable: the lost-sensor fallback.

protection.name: Protections
protection.description: Windows, frozen thermometer, zone valve, return limit.

data.window_drop_entities: Open window from a fast temperature drop – thermometers to watch (near the windows)
data.frozen_after_h: Frozen room thermometer: hours with an unchanged value
data.frozen_burn_min: Frozen room thermometer: minutes of heat meanwhile
data.valve_feedback_entity: Valve feedback (end switch or valve position, if there is one)
data.zone_own_mixer: Has its own mixing loop (the floor is protected whatever the boiler sends)
data.valve_exercise: Summer valve exercise (when closed for a week)
data.return_max: Return limit (0 = none): the valve stays closed above it
data.return_hysteresis: Return limit releases this far below

data_description.frozen_after_h: When the room thermometer has shown exactly the same value for this many hours while the heat ran at least the minutes below, the reading counts as frozen and the fallback runs. 0 = off. In the measured house the thermometer stayed unchanged for at most 1.4 h while heating.
data_description.frozen_burn_min: The heat must have run at least this long in the unchanged time: a real room warms by at least one step from that much heat.
data_description.valve_feedback_entity: The central boiler uses it to see whether the valve is really open (on/off, open/closed or at least 20 %). Empty or unavailable: it counts with the actuator opening time.
data_description.zone_own_mixer: Off: the flow of a central modulating boiler never goes above the highest flow of this zone (flow_max, 45 °C for a floor by default) while its circuit can get water – radiator zones heat more weakly then. Switch it on only when the floor circuit really has a mixing valve or a temperature limiter.
data_description.valve_exercise: Once a week it opens a long-closed valve for a few minutes so it does not seize. The zone asks for no heat meanwhile, a central boiler does not start.

data.floor_hysteresis: Back on this far below the limit

data.floor_temper_offset: Floor target above the room target (0 = by the floor covering)
data.floor_temper_night: Floor target at night / in the sleep preset (0 = as by day)

data.floor_temper_room_margin: No tempering once the room is this much above its target

data.floor_cooling: Floor cooling in summer (reversible heat pump)
data.dew_margin: Safety margin above the dew point
data.cool_flow_entity: Cooling flow setpoint (optional; else the heating one)

data_description.floor_max: No heat above it, whatever the regulator says. 0 = by the covering and the sensor position: under the covering 29 °C for tiles, 27 °C for wood, laminate, vinyl, carpet; in the screed between the pipes 29 / 33 / 31 (vinyl) °C; above a supply pipe 36 °C. An electric floor always uses the under-covering value. Without a covering: 27 °C for an electric floor, 29 °C for a water floor.
data_description.floor_covering: Gives the floor limit (with the sensor position) and the tempering offset: tiles 2 °C, other coverings 3 °C.
data_description.floor_probe: A sensor deeper in the screed reads warmer than the surface, so its limit is higher. The deeper positions' limits (screed 31–33 °C, above a pipe 36 °C) are estimates: they do not guarantee a surface below 27 °C. Under wood, parquet and laminate a sensor right under the covering (surface) is recommended.
data_description.floor_temper: Comfort: a warm floor. While the room is warm enough the floor is held at the room target + the offset (by the floor sensor); it stops when the room gets this much above its target. The floor limit always wins. Needs a floor sensor.
data_description.floor_temper_room_margin: Default 0.5 °C. A larger value gives a warmer floor, but the room swings further above its target and uses more energy.
data_description.floor_fallback: Instead of the blind demand (or, for an electric floor, no heat) the floor is held at the room target + the tempering offset while the room thermometer is silent. Without a floor reading it works as before.

devices.name: Heat source signals and power
devices.description: Burner signal, power draw, output, heat pump and electric signals.

data.flame_entity: Flame sensor (real burner state, e.g. from the boiler's power draw)
data.boiler_power_entity: Boiler power sensor (W) – for the boiler health
data.power_idle_w: Below this power the boiler stands by
data.power_burn_w: From this power the burner burns (below it only the pump runs)
data.boiler_power_kw: Boiler output (0 = heat need is not used in regulation)
data.load_limit_kw: Shared power limit of the electric zones (kW, 0 = none; the same on every zone)
data.power_available_entity: Controlled power signal (optional: on = power available)

data_description.power_idle_w: Below this the boiler stands by. Leave the defaults (20 W / 115 W) untouched and the boiler health only learns – it judges "no response" / "no flame" by the power draw once you give your boiler's own values.
data_description.power_burn_w: At or above this the burner burns (between the two: only the pump runs).
data_description.load_limit_kw: Give the zone's own power in the boiler power field (for electric heat: the heater's). If switching on would exceed the limit, the zone waits and its cycle starts later – the zones heat staggered. Counts in live mode only.
data_description.hp_defrost_entity: While on (or named defrost), fault detection waits and the run does not count as running without command.
data_description.hp_dhw_entity: A 3-way valve or a mode sensor: while it makes hot water the house waits, this is no fault.

measures.name: Measurements (optional)
measures.description: More data about the heat source and the room. HC shows them in the HC info panel, and a value past its limit turns the boiler problem sensor on. They do not change the heating decision.

data.heat_output_entity: Heat given off (heat meter, kWh) – for the COP
data.starts_per_hour_max: Switching too often: more starts than this an hour

data_description.heat_output_entity: The COP is the daily increase of the heat given off over that of the instance's energy meter (power): today, 7 days, the season (from 1 September).
data_description.hp_dhw_entity: While it makes hot water the fault watch pauses; this is no fault.
data_description.fault_code_entity: 0, empty, "ok", "none" = no fault; anything else counts as one.
data_description.humidity_entity: Dew point and mould risk in the instance's room. With several rooms, set them per room in the rooms form.
data_description.radiator_cold_min: When a radiator thermometer stays cold this long while heating and its room is below its target.
data_description.fault_ok_values: Comma separated, e.g. "OK, Normal, 255". All zeros (00, F.00, 0x00) are no fault anyway.

rooms.title: Rooms – areas
rooms.description:
Tick the Home Assistant areas that are rooms of this boiler; next to each is what I found there. Unticking one removes the room (and its HC thermostat); the TRV heads are left alone. You can change this any time.

Now:
{rooms_en}<!-- {rooms_hu} -->

data.custom_rooms: New room without an area (name; several separated by commas)

data_description.home_name: Shown in the HC info house drawing (empty: the instance's name).

room_details.title: Rooms – settings
room_details.description:
One fold-out per room: the area's devices as check boxes (ticked already for a new room).
- Several thermometers: their mean counts and HC makes a group thermometer for it; presence and window: any of them.
- Leading room: its thermometer drives the boiler. TRV room: its heads get the room's target; its window closes only its own heads. Room without a TRV (watched): heated only through the boiler, its window stops the boiler.
- "Add another device": from another area; HC sorts it where it belongs.
- Presence: a room tracker (its state is the room's area, e.g. Bermuda) or a motion / occupancy sensor. Nobody there for the given minutes: the room's target goes down by the setback (never below the frost limit).

{rooms_en}<!-- {rooms_hu} -->

data.confirm: Yes, the leading room has a TRV head (it gets the house target)
data.room_tolerance: Valve advice tolerance (room's deviation from the house)

room_own.title: Rooms – own schedule
room_own.description:
The temperatures and night of the rooms set to their own schedule. On a household vacation the house's vacation target counts.

data.flow_setpoint_entity: Flow setpoint entity (number / input_number, e.g. OpenTherm or ebusd)

data_description.demand_entity: A dry-contact wall thermostat read through a binary sensor, input boolean or switch: on = heat, off = no heat; then the room thermometer is optional. Frost, window, summer rest, the floor limit and floor tempering still apply. Unavailable: the lost-sensor fallback.

error.confirm_active: Confirm your choice for active mode.
error.humidity_required: Floor cooling needs a humidity sensor (no cooling without a dew point).
error.buffer_order: The stop temperature must be above the start temperature.
error.demand_required: This instance has no room thermometer: the wall thermostat contact is required.
error.climate_taken: This climate is an HC thermostat or is driven by another HC instance already – two would fight over it.
error.cycle_too_short: The cycle is too short for the useful heat delay: at least the delay + the minimum on + the minimum off time (e.g. 20 minutes for a 10-minute delay with 5 + 5).
error.confirm_required: Confirm your choice for a system that is not recommended.
error.indoor_required: Give a room thermometer or a wall thermostat contact.
error.rooms_need_valves: Rooms work with TPI or PID only. Remove them in the Rooms menu first, then change the control.

options.electric_heater: Electric heater (convector, oil radiator, infrared panel)
options.district_heating: District heating (zone valve or TRV heads)
options.external_heat: Heat source with its own control (zone valve only; PLC, heat pump's own controller)

options.floor_single: Floor only, mixing manifold, one zone
options.mixed_no_circuit: Mixed, no separate circuit, shared flow
options.mixed_mixing: Mixed, mixing circuit with own pump
options.room_unit: Room with its own unit (AC, electric heater)

options.ac: AC: setpoint shift by the room thermometer (virtual i-Feel)

options.next_change: Until the next night start or end

options.standalone: Standalone (one thermostat, own boiler or relay)
options.zone: Zone (switches only its own valve or TRV)
options.buffer: Buffer tank (charges from the heat source)

options.screed: In the screed, between the pipes (estimate)

options.auto: Automatic (by the meter or the heat source)

room_no_target.message: {room}: no TRV head here, the room is heated only through the boiler – set the target on {host} (the room follows the house target).
